papers.summary: For parabolic Ahlfors regular sets, we show that the bilateral weak geometric lemma (BWGL), bilateral approximation by unions of planes (BAUP), and corona decompositions by $Lip$(1,1/2) graphs (whose defining functions need not have half-order time derivatives in BMO) are equivalent. These geometric conditions do not imply the strong geometric lemma. A key tool is a parabolic version of Reifenberg's theorem for sets with holes, which we prove here. As an application of these geometric results, we prove that a parabolic Ahlfors $(n+2)$-regular measure $μ$ on $\mathbb{R}^{d+1}$, $1\leq n\leq d-1$, is parabolic uniformly rectifiable if its support satisfies any of these equivalent conditions and the parabolic Riesz transform is bounded on $L^2(μ)$.
papers.title: Parabolic Reifenberg Parametrizations and Corona Decompositions, with Applications to Singular Integrals

papers.summary: Risk management of worst-of autocallables needs price sensitivities (Greeks) up to third order and the potential future exposure, a tail quantile of the note's future value. In Monte Carlo, each order of differentiation multiplies the sampling noise by a factor that grows with the observation frequency, and nested simulation turns the noise of its inner paths into a bias of the quantile. We instead solve the backward pricing recursion, storing the continuation value as an $hp$ functional tensor train (hp-FTT) whose piecewise-polynomial cores are split at the barriers, so that worst-of barrier events act exactly, with rank one. For Gaussian transitions we show that the polynomial degree sufficient for an error $\varepsilon$ grows only as $\sqrt{\log(1/\varepsilon)}$. One solve then gives every Greek at any spot without sampling noise, by integrating the likelihood-ratio weight against the stored value, and the values it stores at future dates replace inner simulation. Against the strongest Monte Carlo estimators we could build or find published, on worst-of autocallables observed monthly on three to five assets, the order of the Greek and the accuracy decide which method is cheaper. At $1\%$ accuracy Monte Carlo is more than an order of magnitude cheaper for deltas, second-order Greeks go either way, and hp-FTT is cheaper for every third-order Greek, by up to two orders of magnitude. At $0.1\%$ hp-FTT is cheaper for every Greek we could check, under geometric Brownian motion and local volatility alike. For the exposure alone Monte Carlo is cheaper at $1\%$ and hp-FTT at $0.1\%$, and a solve run for the Greeks yields it for little more than scenario sampling. Sampling pays in variance for each derivative and hp-FTT in rank for each asset, so Monte Carlo keeps low-order Greeks at percent accuracy, rarely observed contracts and many assets.
papers.title: Functional Tensor Trains for High-Order Greeks and Exposure Tails of Multi-Asset Structured Products

papers.summary: The thin-film equation describes the evolution of a thin liquid film driven by capillarity and limited by viscosity. For sufficiently small film heights, thermal fluctuations may not be neglected. Since the thin-film equation as an overdamped evolution equation has a gradient flow structure, the informal implementation of the fluctuation-dissipation principle is straightforward. In this paper, we work out that the concept of Dirichlet forms and the related construction of Markov processes are tailor-made for this type of overdamped continuum evolution with thermal noise. However, the concept of Dirichlet forms relies on the availability of a Gibbsian equilibrium measure, which, in case of the thin-film equation, limits the treatment to the $(1+1)$-dimensional case. By means of Dirichlet form theory, we obtain the existence and uniqueness of the evolution of laws on configuration space. We show that the regularity of the realizations of this Markov process matches the heuristics. In a simplified situation with a Gaussian reference measure and a non-degenerate mobility function, we characterize it as what is called an energy solution. The latter provides a pathwise decomposition of the driving forces into a deterministic and a thermal one, which was the starting point. Applying the same techniques in the spatially discretized setting proposed in [Math. Comp. 92 (2023), 1931--1976], we obtain the same results uniformly in the discretization parameter. In particular, Galerkin as well as spectral approximations of the stochastic thin-film equation are shown to be uniformly tight in optimal topologies. In the simplified setting, we also prove Mosco convergence of the associated Dirichlet forms and thereby obtain convergence of these approximations.
papers.title: Dirichlet form approach to stochastic thin-film equations

papers.summary: For stochastic matrices of order $n$, the Karpelevič region is the set of all possible eigenvalues. We study matrices whose first and last $m$ rows are arbitrary probability vectors, while the remaining middle rows come from one probability vector by successive cyclic shifts to the right, moving the last entry to the first position each time. As $m$ increases, their eigenvalue regions expand from the polygon spanned by the $n$th roots of unity. For $n\ge3$, they first equal the full Karpelevič region at $m=\lceil(n-1)/4\rceil$. Reproducing all $n$ eigenvalues, counted with multiplicity, of every stochastic matrix of the same order requires $m=\lfloor n/2\rfloor$. Thus, in even order $n\ge4$, retaining two consecutive rows with the Toeplitz pattern can exclude eigenvalue lists even when every possible eigenvalue occurs individually. The boundary of the Karpelevič region consists of arcs joining roots of unity. We determine the least $m$ for which every point of each arc occurs as an eigenvalue in our family. For arcs whose nonreal points first become possible eigenvalues at order $n\ge4$, and for $m\ge1$ below this minimum, no point on the arc other than its endpoints occurs in the family. At the minimum, every point on the arc becomes attainable. At the smallest order $n\ge4$ at which a nonreal point on a boundary arc away from its endpoints can occur as an eigenvalue, that point determines the characteristic polynomial of every stochastic matrix of order $n$ having it as an eigenvalue. Further results describe the smaller regions and the angles at which their boundaries approach roots of unity.
papers.title: Spectra of stochastic matrices with a Toeplitz interior

papers.summary: We consider the adjoint-free random-plane iteration algorithm for finding the top eigenvector of a matrix proposed in (SIAM J. Matrix Anal. Appl. 47 (2026), 1349-1374). Unlike standard methods such as the power method or gradient descent, the above algorithm lacked linear convergence guarantees in the presence of a spectral gap. In this paper, we establish explicit spectral-gap-dependent global linear convergence rates in expectation, providing quantitative guarantees for the empirically observed convergence.
papers.title: Stochastic Rayleigh-Ritz Ascent: Global Linear Convergence under a Spectral Gap

papers.summary: Let $d\ge2$ and $t>0$. We study the bilinear triangle averaging operator $$\mathcal T_t(f,g)(x)=\int_{\mathcal I}f(x-ty)g(x-tz) dσ(y,z),$$ where $σ$ is the normalized surface measure on the manifold $\mathcal I=\{(y,z)\in\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^d:|y|=|z|=|y-z|=1\}$ of equilateral triangles of side length one with a vertex at the origin. We prove the strong-type asymmetric $L^p$-improving estimate $$\mathcal T_1:L^{\frac{d+1}{d-1}}(\mathbb R^d)\times L^{\frac{d^2-1}{d^2-3d+4}}(\mathbb R^d)\longrightarrow L^{\frac{d+1}{2}}(\mathbb R^d)$$ in every dimension $d\ge4$. This enlarges the range of exponents $(p,q,r)$ for which the triangle averaging operator is known to map $L^p(\mathbb R^d)\times L^q(\mathbb R^d)$ to $L^r(\mathbb R^d)$, and symmetrization produces new symmetric estimates in every such dimension as well. The proof combines Sobolev smoothing estimates, obtained through a microlocal decomposition of the triangle incidence relation, with complex interpolation in an analytic family of averages over triangles of varying shape that contains the triangle averaging operator. We also establish maximal estimates for triangle averages. Let $E\subset[1,2]$ be a nonempty set of upper Minkowski dimension $β$, and let $\mathcal T_E(f,g)=\sup_{t\in E}|\mathcal T_t(f,g)|$. We prove that $$\|\mathcal T_E(f,g)\|_2\lesssim\|f\|_{H^{-s_1}}\|g\|_{H^{-s_2}}$$ whenever $s_1,s_2\ge0$, $s_1+s_2<\frac{d-3-β}{2}$ and $d>3+β$. This improves the previously known Sobolev smoothing estimate by half a derivative and lowers the dimension requirement. We also obtain asymmetric localized maximal estimates of the form $\mathcal T_E:L^p(\mathbb R^d)\times L^q(\mathbb R^d)\to L^r(\mathbb R^d)$ in an enlarged range of exponents.
papers.title: Asymmetric $L^p$-improving and maximal estimates for the triangle averaging operator

papers.summary: In this paper we present a method to effectively and efficiently provide pathwise approximations of the Riemannian Brownian motion on a reductive homogeneous space $M\cong G/H$ endowed with a $G$-invariant metric. This setting includes spheres, hyperbolic spaces, the space of symmetric positive-definite matrices, flag manifolds and Stiefel manifolds. The simulation is based on Wong--Zakai approximations of an appropriately chosen SDE in $G$ that is projected down onto $M\cong G/H$. The effectiveness lies in the fact that well-established results on the convergence rate of the Wong--Zakai equation immediately carry over to the homogeneous space thanks to Nash's embedding. The efficiency lies in the fact that explicit representations of the Wong--Zakai approximations can be obtained in this setting using the Lie exponential map.
papers.title: Stochastic processes on reductive homogeneous and symmetric spaces

papers.summary: We construct an explicit 64-point subset of $\mathbb F_2^9$ which tiles by translation but has no linear-subspace tiling complement. Together with our earlier dimension-eight theorem and a product argument, this shows that every nonempty tile in $\mathbb F_2^d$ has a linear-subspace complement precisely when $d\le8$. The example is spectral, so it is not a counterexample to Fuglede's conjecture. Its construction uses six three-dimensional subspaces of $\mathbb F_2^6$, specified by a small table. We classify all its tiling complements and spectra: there are exactly 512 complements and 64 spectra, with one translation class of each. Every spectrum has normalized Wiener norm $15/8$. An appendix proves that Goyal's related construction is affinely inequivalent but has the same tiling complements and spectra. The construction and both classifications are proved from first principles. We also give elementary proofs of the positive assertion in dimensions at most seven and for all tile sizes other than sixteen in dimension eight. The remaining case uses our previously established theorem based on the classification of perfect binary codes of length fifteen.
papers.title: Tiling without a subspace complement: a sharp counterexample in dimension nine over the field with two elements

papers.summary: We present a high-order, positivity preserving, and asymptotic preserving approximation of the gray radiative transfer equations. The time and space approximation is done using a diagonally-implicit Runge-Kutta method with stabilized, continuous finite elements, and the angular approximation uses the method of discrete ordinates. We detail a simple and robust inner/outer iteration strategy to solve these equations and prove that the proposed scheme is exactly conservative, independent of iterative tolerances. A maximum and minimum principle is enforced using a conservative redistribution limiting technique, and the method is demonstrated to be robust in the thick diffusion limit.
papers.title: A Robust High-order Approximation of the Gray Thermal Radiative Transfer Equations

papers.summary: We prove that KP, with Full Set Induction, is neither solid nor tight. More generally, every consistent theory obtained from KPC by adding a quantifier bounded set of sentences has a model with a parameter-free definable class surjection from its natural numbers onto its universe. Using such enumerations to define generic extensions by relative interpretations, we show that theories with the stable definable ground property are not tight. Ground definability over MOST and continuum coding over ZFC^{Π_3} yield applications to weak inductive set theories with large cardinals and forcing axioms. Finally, solidity for quantifier bounded extensions of MOST with Full Set Induction implies a Ground Axiom formulated using a fixed finite level of genericity; under the same solidity hypothesis, the corresponding extension of full ZFC proves the ordinary Ground Axiom.
papers.title: Loose Inductive Set Theories

papers.summary: Let $p$ be a prime number and let $K$ be a field such that $p$ is prime to the absolute Galois group $\operatorname{Gal}(K)$, in the sense that $p$ does not divide the degree of any finite Galois extension of $K$. We conjecture that $K$ is large in the sense of Pop: any smooth algebraic curve $C$ over $K$ with a $K$-rational point has infinitely many $K$-rational points. This conjecture would have some consequences in mathematical logic. For instance, it would imply the expected classification of stable fields of positive characteristic. We give some weak evidence for this conjecture. Specifically, suppose that $K$ is a perfect field and $\operatorname{Gal}(K)$ is prime to $p$. Then every abelian variety $A$ over $K$ has Zariski dense $K$-rational points, and if $C$ is a smooth curve of genus less than $7-p$ with at least one $K$-rational point, then $C$ has infinitely many $K$-rational points.
papers.title: A conjecture on Galois groups and large fields

papers.summary: We consider noncommutative analogues of associated fibre bundles where the total space, base space and even the fiber may be nonaffine, that is, not represented by a single algebra, and where the structure group is replaced by a Hopf algebra $H$. We choose to describe gluing of affine pieces by corings. In the role of a principal bundle we take an internal $E$-coring $M$ in the monoidal category of right $H$-comodules where $E$ is a faithfully flat right Hopf-Galois extension. In a role of a fibre we either take a left $H$-comodule algebra $F$, or more generally an internal $F$-coring $N$ in the monoidal category of left $H$-comodules. Cotensor products combining these data is used to obtain an ordinary coring representing the total space of an associated bundle. If the fiber coring $N$ is equipped with a choice of an $H$-coinvariant grouplike element, then we exhibit a canonical morphisms of corings from the $H$-coinvariant coring of $M$ to the associated bundle coring which is viewed as a dual to the projection of an associated bundle.
papers.title: Coring morphisms presenting nonaffine noncommutative fibre bundles

papers.summary: We prove that a finite-dimensional connected monomial algebra over an algebraically closed field is derived tame if and only if every finite connected convex subcategory of its universal cover has non-negative Euler form. Derived tameness is also equivalent to tameness of its repetitive category and trivial extension. For one-cycle algebras, this condition is equivalent to the non-negativity on $\mathbb R$ of $|Q_0|$ explicitly computable polynomials in $\mathbb Q[t]$. This gives a finite algorithm for deciding derived tameness. We also construct an infinite family of derived-tame one-cycle string algebras with minimal cubic relations, no two of which are derived equivalent.
papers.title: Derived tame monomial algebras

papers.summary: Elliptic Fekete configurations minimize logarithmic energy on the sphere. They also provide a natural source of complex polynomials with controlled Shub--Smale condition number. The link between these two problems is the product of the distances from each point to all the other points: logarithmic energy controls the geometric mean of these products, whereas local conditioning depends on each product separately. This paper studies the passage from global information to uniform estimates at individual nodes, exploring its connections with quantitative equidistribution, Riesz energies, and polynomial conditioning. We improve separation bounds for elliptic Fekete configurations and obtain quantitative Riesz-energy estimates for both these configurations and spherical roots of polynomials with optimal-order global conditioning. For $0<s<2$, these estimates also improve explicit upper bounds for the minimal Riesz $s$-energy.
papers.title: Elliptic Fekete points: separation, Riesz energies, and polynomial conditioning

papers.summary: This paper introduces the ${\rm P}$-generalized determinant, a more general class of quaternion determinants. It unifies several classical quaternion determinants proposed between 1922 and 2008, including the Moore determinant, the Xie determinant, the Chen determinant, and the Kyrchei row--column determinants, thereby revealing the essential nature of quaternion determinants as multivariate polynomial-type functions with a fixed ordering of products. We provide equivalent characterizations of the expansion of the $\mathrm{P}$-generalized determinant along a given row or column, and establish conversion relations between the $\mathrm{P}_{l}$- and $\mathrm{P}_{r}$-generalized determinants. We prove that the $\mathrm{P}$-generalized determinant of a quaternion Hermitian matrix is a real number independent of the choice of cycle representation rule. We further investigate the behavior of the $\mathrm{P}$-generalized determinant under elementary row and column operations on quaternion Hermitian matrices, as well as its linearity in rows and columns. Finally, using the $\mathrm{P}$-generalized determinant, we derive determinantal representations of the inverse of an invertible quaternion Hermitian matrix and of the unique solution to the quaternion matrix equation $AXB=C$. In particular, this yields Cramer's rule for the left and right linear systems $Ax=b$ and $xA=b$.
papers.title: P-generalized determinant over quaternions and its applications

papers.summary: In this paper, we study quasi-projective dimensions of modules over rings connected by homological ring epimorphisms. We establish several inequalities relating the quasi-projective dimensions over the source and target rings. As applications, we investigate the quasi-global dimension of triangular matrix rings and provide examples showing that the class of modules with finite quasi-projective dimension does not satisfy the 2-out-of-3 property in general.
papers.title: Quasi-projective dimensions over homological ring epimorphisms

papers.summary: We study the truncated Dirichlet functional \[ Φ_n (f) = \sum_{k = 1}^n k |a_k|^2, \quad f(z) = \sum_{k = 0}^\infty a_k z^k, \] when $f$ belongs to the Bloch space. If $n \geq 27$, we find a normalized Bloch function $f_n$ such that \[ Φ_n (f_n) > n B_n^2, \] where $B_n = \max \{ |a_n| : \| f \|_{\mathcal{B}} = 1 \}$, thus proving that an inequality by Kayumov and Wirths cannot be extended to large values of $n$. Nevertheless, we show that the inequality $Φ_n(f) \leq n B_n^2$ holds for all normalized functions when $n \leq 9$.
papers.title: Truncated Dirichlet estimates for Bloch functions

papers.summary: Let $K$ be a field which is strongly stable, that is, stable and strongly dependent. Then $K$ is finite or algebraically closed. This answers a question of Shelah.
papers.title: Strongly stable fields

papers.summary: Many explicit constructions in algebra are not first-order definable in classical finitary logic, but are, however, definable in infinitary logic. The aim of this paper is to show how infinitary logic can be used to lift model-theoretic results in arithmetic to a quantifier-sensitive form. We apply this idea to a deep result of Jahnke and Kartas on the model theory of perfectoid fields. Our main result is that a first-order sentence $φ$ holds in the tilt $k^{\flat}$ of a perfectoid field $k$ if and only if a certain sentence $φ^{\natural}$ holds in a non-principal ultrapower of $k$, where $φ^{\natural}$ does not depend on $k$ and is only slightly more complicated than $φ$ itself. In particular, tilting preserves the Lévy hierarchy in a precise sense. To this end, we prove that the Standard Decomposition of a valued field at a constant $t$ is infinitarily interpretable by formulas of rank at most 1.
papers.title: The complexity of tilting

papers.summary: We prove quantitative sub-ballisticity for the self-avoiding walk on the lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$, $d\geq 2$. Namely, we obtain an explicit exponential rate of decay for the probability that a self-avoiding walk of length $n$ reaches distance at least $vn$, in terms of $v>0$. As a consequence, we show that the displacement of an $n$-step self-avoiding walk is at most $n/\exp(c\log^* n)$ with very high probability. Previously, only a non-quantitative $o(n)$ bound was known from the work of Duminil-Copin and Hammond. Along the way, we show that at criticality the partition function of bridges of length $n$ is on average bounded by $C/\log\log n$, which we believe to be of independent interest. Our approach is based on a quantitative analysis of the original nonconstructive proof of Duminil-Copin and Hammond using ideas from proof theory.
papers.title: Quantitative sub-ballisticity of self-avoiding walk on $\mathbb{Z}^d$
